_about: Storms kept as validation cases (John, Nov 16 2026). Truth is the Mint gauge (SFOC1) only. Times UTC; local is America/Los_Angeles. tools/validate_cases.py scores each case from the data branch; 'expect' is what a correct forecast system should have done, used to judge future changes. Nothing here tunes a forecast.

cases.local: Sun Nov 15, 1 PM – Mon 2 AM PT

observed.level_reached: drains working hard (one hour >= 0.20"); never falling behind or driveway

forecast_as_issued.heavy_hour_2pm: primary 0.06–0.08" with 2–3% of runs heavy at 1–6 h; best single source HRRR 0.10" (1–3 h); every source low
forecast_as_issued.total: 0.64–0.70" predicted at 1–12 h (good); onset within 0–1 h (good)
forecast_as_issued.false_alarm_midnight: 08 UTC: radar nowcast 0.38" (98% heavy), pushed heavy 85%, drains-falling-behind 46%, driveway 30%; ensemble 0.03", HRRR 0.00", gauge last hour 0.07"

expect: radar alone does not raise drains-falling-behind or driveway at 08 UTC (tests/test_radar_safeguard.py)
heavy-hour miss at 22 UTC stays visible in the 1–3 h and 3–6 h scorecards until a change, reviewed by John, fixes it

cases.local: Tue Nov 17 10 PM – Thu Nov 19 8 AM PT

forecast_as_issued.card: hazard flood (15:32 UTC run): heaviest hour most likely Wed 7–8 AM PT, possible 0.20" (~0.17"/hr), about 1.92" through Thu 8 AM
forecast_as_issued.heavy_share: 60% of runs have a 0.20" hour; primary hours 12–18 UTC at 0.16–0.17"/h with 27–41% heavy

expect: score onset, peak timing, heavy hours and total against SFOC1 at 1–3 h and 3–6 h, and the card's gear (data/cards) hour by hour
any Sandbags or driveway push must have corroboration recorded (levels.corroborated) if it came from a radar-primary hour
radar-only heavy pushes read 'Heavy rain possible in the next hour'; review every push sent against the gauge and the card's words (data/cards) after the storm
prospective case: no model, threshold or weighting change before the storm is observed and reviewed (John, Nov 16)
